note: The spec's worked example (section 2): the pull request title in a shell, node:latest, curl | bash and the tj-actions pin into ci/build, which holds a read token and no secret, so every path there is code execution, High, one per subject (the forbidden tag and the missing digest of node:latest anchor one path together); node:latest is only not pinned, so the dependency cap holds its path at Medium, while the fetched script is no reference to pin and stays High. The tj-actions pin is a full commit SHA: offline the advisory is not fetched, and the unauthorized source alone is no entry (nothing changes without a commit here), so it is an other finding at High; with the advisory it would anchor a High path, the unauthorized source joining it. plumber.yml runs on push to main with id-token: write and security-events: write: a write token, but no signing or release step, so no impact, and the unprotected main anchors an unprotected_push path into it that is High (a token, no impact) and could never be Critical (a push entry is capped at High). The getplumber/plumber action is SHA-pinned from a default trusted owner, so it anchors nothing. Hand count: three High paths (the unprotected_push path, the pull request title and the fetched script into ci/build) 3 x 15 = 45, one Medium path (node:latest) 6, one other finding, the unauthorized source at High 10 (the persisted credentials on plumber/plumber ride the push path), so the high, medium and low items count 61, under the 69 they count for at most, and 100 - 61 = 39, no Critical path: D.
